notes.text: Requires the WordPress Manager cPanel plugin, available from WordPress Manager 3.0. The site argument, where present, is the caller-selected WordPress URL without a protocol prefix and may contain a path. No site value is inferred. The client does not poll SSE paths or fetch archive URLs.

All documented response object fields are optional. Omission is distinct from explicit null, empty lists and zero flags. Integer flags remain 0|1 without string or boolean normalization. This method is explicitly read-only in the pinned source and uses GET.

The pinned formal data schema declares an optional items property containing RestoreInProgress or RestoreNotInProgress. Preserve that nesting and merge their optional object fields without discarding last_outcome. sites retains the documented list-of-records or opaque-object alternatives; empty objects/lists and unknown opaque fields are preserved. The source describes restore-process IDs as unimplemented/null-only, while the formal id schema remains nullable string. last_outcome.error is nullable string; status is text and have_outcome is an integer flag. No completed restoration is inferred from any_running=0 alone.

The pinned full response examples place any_running, sites and last_outcome directly under data, while the formal schema nests these fields under data.items. This unresolved source discrepancy is tracked under whm-api-client-8x0.2.32. The generated contract follows the formal nesting and does not infer flat fields from the examples; successful API status alone does not establish compatibility with either live variant.

Cleans temporary system resources after restoration. The data is an integer 0|1 flag, with 0 meaning unsuccessful cleanup. It is distinct from the UAPI envelope status. Null and absent payloads are mismatches; cleanup is not a promise to undo restored files or to delete archives.

backupPath is the path to an existing server-side backup archive, forwarded unchanged as backup_path, not a local file upload. Starts restoration of the selected site and returns an optional restore_id. The source declares no rollback. Restoration changes site state and its process ID alone does not establish completion.
